# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

# Memory Index

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).
- [Prove With the Real Tool](feedback_prove_with_the_real_tool.md) — Fake-tool tests and clean compiles hid the 0.10.1 gh credential regression; reproduce auth/release/registry paths with the real tool, test the failing case first, state what is unproven.
- [Callisto Self-Release Incident — Durable Memory](project_release_self_hosting_incident_2026-09.md) — Claude invented and later misattributed the release approval gate, misunderstood rerun semantics, and repeatedly declared fixes before publication; records non-negotiable policy, verified failures, corrective architecture, and required incident protocol.
- [Hardcoded Values — Proactive Search Required](feedback_hardcoded_values.md) — User repeatedly frustrated by missed hardcoded values; always include a dedicated pass in any audit or fix session.
- [Track 0: gix WASI spike — NO-GO verdict](project_track0_wasi_verdict.md) — mmap ENOSYS in WASI blocks all gix object reads; callisto-moon exec-seam must use warpgate_pdk::exec_command.
- [Publish Pipeline Audit — 38 bugs, fix ordering, semantic coupling map](project_publish_pipeline_audit.md) — Full adversarial audit complete; 5 P0s, 11 P1s, 15+ P2s; three root patterns; phased fix sequence with dependency order.
- [Parallel Fixing Anti-Pattern](feedback_parallel_fixing.md) — Parallel agents for fixes fail on semantically coupled systems even across different files; use parallel for investigation only.
- [Validate Each Fix Individually](feedback_validate_each_fix.md) — Run targeted tests after every individual fix; do not batch changes and rely solely on final CI run.
- Architecture: ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/architecture/ (moved from .claude/semantic-model on 2026-09-25) — read before implementation work.
- [Active Work](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) — Tracks B, E, F (resolve_package_config), G (callisto matrix) all shipped and passing just ci. Pipeline: canon→vector→lambda.
- [Canon Pipeline Scope](feedback_canon_pipeline_scope.md) — Skip canon ceremony for targeted bug fixes with RED tests already written; canon auditor loops infinitely on implementation-detail prose.
- [Workspace Audit 2026-08](project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md) — CLOSED: 8-dimension audit, all critical/high + all 31 medium/low findings re-verified fixed as of 2026-08-27.
- [Found Code Needs Same Rigor](feedback_found_code_needs_same_rigor.md) — Committing pre-existing uncommitted code after only "compiles + existing tests pass" missed a zero-test-coverage regression; found/inherited code needs the same TDD/adversarial rigor as freshly-written code.
- [Manifest Persist Track](project_manifest_persist_track.md) — Both Spec A (mutate/persist split) and Spec B (write-batching) shipped; the apply_version_plan redundant-open/persist audit finding is fully closed.
- [Reviewer Must Actually Run Checks](feedback_reviewer_must_actually_run_checks.md) — lambda-reviewer falsely reported clippy clean once; always instruct review agents to run commands for real, not infer results.
- [Iterate Reviews in Foreground](feedback_iterate_reviews_in_foreground.md) — Background agent notifications were unreliable across a multi-round spec/plan review loop; user called it out twice — run tight revise-review cycles in the foreground.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

17	3. **Verify before reporting**: Try to disprove the finding first (check for a guard you may have missed). Give a concrete failing scenario (specific input, state, or flag). Mark `CONFIRMED` (path fully traced) or `PLAUSIBLE` (strong signal, not fully traced).
18	4. **Structured Reporting**: Use the format in `../skills/bug-hunter/SKILL.md` — Status, Location (`file:line`), Classification, Root Cause, Failing Scenario, Severity, Verification Strategy.
19	5. **Sibling sweep, not single hit**: When a confirmed defect is one instance of a structurally repeated pattern (same algorithm reimplemented per ecosystem/mode/branch), grep for every other instance before reporting it as one finding. List all sibling locations in the same finding and note whether the fix should be "patch each copy" or "unify into one implementation" — the latter is preferred whenever N>1 copies exist. A finding that names only the first instance you tripped over, when siblings exist, is an incomplete finding.

1	---
2	name: bug-hunter
3	description: >-
4	  Universal, repo-agnostic Rust bug hunting framework. Finds silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, ordering/staleness bugs, crash-safety violations, and edge cases across any Rust codebase using Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning.
5	---
6	
7	# Universal Rust Bug-Hunter Skill
8	
9	## Goal
10	
11	Find real bugs before they ship in any Rust repository (monorepos, CLI engines, libraries, polyglot WASM plugins): silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, data corruption, ordering staleness, crash-safety violations, and edge cases that break production.
12	
13	This skill is **Rigid**: follow it exactly across any Rust workspace.
14	
15	## The Law
16	
17	> NO FINDING MARKED `CONFIRMED` WITHOUT AN END-TO-END TRACE. NO FIX MARKED DONE WITHOUT A TEST THAT FAILED BEFORE THE FIX AND PASSES AFTER, RUN IN THIS SESSION.
18	
19	## Core Rules
20	
21	- **Verify by Tracing**: Don't trust a comment, docstring, passing test, or a prior audit's "FIXED" label. Trace the code execution path yourself.
22	- **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: When executing multi-agent bug hunts, DO NOT partition subagents by directory or crate names. ALWAYS partition subagents by **Hazard Taxonomy** or **Code Smell Sweep** across the entire workspace.
23	- **Strict Invariants**: Prioritize data integrity, crash-safety, error propagation, and security bugs over style or refactoring.
24	- **Read-Only Investigation**: Investigate and report findings first. Do not mutate files unless explicitly requested to apply fixes.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## The 6 Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies
29	
30	1. **Discarded Data & Unused CLI / Struct Parameters**: Leading-underscore parameters (`_opts`, `_config`), unused Clap CLI flags.
31	2. **Ordering, Mutability & Fixpoint Staleness**: First-write-wins vs max-value-wins, graph solver loops missing re-enqueueing logic.
32	3. **Spec-vs-Code Compliance Drift**: Requirements in design docs/specs missing enforcement logic in functions.
33	4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
34	5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
35	6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## The 6 Architectural Code Smells & Ripgrep Sweeps
40	
41	1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
42	2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.
43	3. **Lossy Serde / CST Formatting Smell**: Replacing TOML/JSON nodes without preserving `.decor()` or line endings.
44	4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
45	5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.
46	6. **Hardcoded Constant Dummy Smell**: Inserting placeholder strings (`"Release update"`, `"changeset.md"`) masking user metadata.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 7 Shared Trait Centralization Framework
51	
52	When auditing multi-crate workspaces, map recurring defects directly to 7 Centralized Rust Traits:
53	1. `PackageIdentityResolver`: Cross-ecosystem package matching and bare name resolution.
54	2. `VersionSpecRenderer`: Format & precision-preserving version requirement rendering.
55	3. `ChangesetStorage`: Crash-safe, transactional disk engine with parent directory fsync.
56	4. `CstManifestEditor`: CST format-preserving manifest modification (`toml_edit` and `serde_json`).
57	5. `GitVcsProvider`: Safe Git tags, shallow checkout handling, and bounded revwalk.
58	6. `CascadeSolver`: Fixpoint dependency graph solver & convergence tracking.
59	7. `ReportPresenter`: Unified text & JSON report renderer with rich `miette` diagnostic cards.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## Hazard-Taxonomy Multi-Agent Dispatch Matrix
64	
65	| Agent Role | Scope | Objective |
66	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
67	| **`bug-hunter-scanner-rust`** | Taxonomies 1 & 4 | Scan workspace for unused CLI flags, discarded parameters, and silent `unwrap_or` defaults. |
68	| **`bug-hunter-adversary-rust`** | Taxonomies 2 & 3 | Trace execution paths end-to-end, disprove candidate signals, and check graph solver fixpoints and spec drift. |
69	| **`bug-hunter-remediator-rust`** | Taxonomies 5 & 6 | Audit boundary inputs, atomic write `.flush()`/`.sync_all()`, write failing regression tests (red), apply fixes. |
70	| **`bug-hunter-architect-rust`** | Smells 1-6 & Trait Centralization | Analyze recurring defect patterns, cluster code smells, and design lean Rust traits with formal contracts. |
71	| **`bug-hunter-mutator-rust`** | Mutation Testing & Coverage | Run `cargo-mutants`, find survived mutant branches, and write boundary unit tests ensuring assertions fail when code is mutated. |
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Evaluation Output Standard
76	
77	Report each confirmed finding in this standard technical format:
78	
79	```markdown
80	### [Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low] <Brief Vulnerability Title>
81	
82	- **Status**: CONFIRMED (execution path fully traced, file:line cited) | PLAUSIBLE (strong signal, not fully traced)
83	- **Location**: `path/to/file.rs:L123-L135`
84	- **Classification**: [Discarded Parameter | Fixpoint Staleness | Spec Drift | Silent Fallback | Boundary Condition | I/O Safety]
85	- **Root Cause**: Concise explanation of the flaw in the current implementation logic.
86	- **Failing Scenario**: Concrete payload, CLI command, or input state that triggers the defect.
87	- **Verification Strategy**: A test that fails on current code and passes once fixed.
88	```

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged managed release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Install registry test tools
        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Verify workflow contracts and reject mutable action references
        run: just workflow-contracts

  recovery-checks:
    name: Check release workflow policy for recovery
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_source_sha != ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install ripgrep
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Verify release workflow contracts
        run: just release-workflow-checks

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, recovery-checks]
    # Exactly one gate runs per event; a failed gate matches neither clause.
    if: >-
      always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      ((needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.recovery-checks.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.recovery-checks.result == 'success' && needs.verify.result == 'skipped'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Attestations are stamped with this run's own SHA, so the
          # coordinator must be exactly the revision running this workflow.
          orchestration_sha="$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
              echo "orchestration_sha=$orchestration_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Interdependent Cargo packages bump together, so Cargo.lock must be refreshed in the release PR.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    # always(): release-candidate's own ancestors include a gate that is skipped
    # by design, and a skipped ancestor silently skips any job without a status function.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The coordinator must be the current workflow revision. Recovery
          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          # Relative name: the consumers verify from a different runner OS and RUNNER_TEMP.
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)
      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Own statement: set -e cannot see a substitution failing inside an echo argument.
          has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          case "$has_artifacts" in
            true|false) ;;
            *) echo "::error::artifact slot probe returned '$has_artifacts'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "has_artifacts=$has_artifacts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build-artifact:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: macos-x64
            runner: macos-14
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"

        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}

        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Assemble attested product artifacts
    needs: [build-artifact, release-candidate, plan]
    if: always() && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' && needs.build-artifact.result == 'success'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      orchestration_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      # Every matrix target's artifact, so a target added to the matrix cannot be built and then left out of the manifest.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: release-build-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - name: Create exact artifact manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    # !cancelled() not always(): a status function still defeats the skipped-ancestor
    # rule, but cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The release-source checkout alone needs Git credentials because
          # graph-owned tag dispatch pushes from this repository.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Downloaded outside the workspace (under $RUNNER_TEMP, like
      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute
      # re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which requires a
      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      # Needs no secrets: a plain tag push with the checkout's Git credentials, like the release tags. A no-op before 1.0.0.
      - name: Move the floating major tag
        working-directory: release-source
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/move-floating-tag.sh" .callisto/release-decision.json cargo/callisto-cli "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          # Per attempt: keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing the prior one.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

toolUseResult.stdout:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged managed release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Install registry test tools
        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Verify workflow contracts and reject mutable action references
        run: just workflow-contracts

  recovery-checks:
    name: Check release workflow policy for recovery
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_source_sha != ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install ripgrep
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Verify release workflow contracts
        run: just release-workflow-checks

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, recovery-checks]
    # Exactly one gate runs per event; a failed gate matches neither clause.
    if: >-
      always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      ((needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.recovery-checks.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.recovery-checks.result == 'success' && needs.verify.result == 'skipped'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Attestations are stamped with this run's own SHA, so the
          # coordinator must be exactly the revision running this workflow.
          orchestration_sha="$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
              echo "orchestration_sha=$orchestration_sha"

      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''

      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      contents: write

        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action

          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    # always(): release-candidate's own ancestors include a gate that is skipped
    # by design, and a skipped ancestor silently skips any job without a status function.

      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'

    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.

        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent

          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}

            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"

      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Own statement: set -e cannot see a substitution failing inside an echo argument.
          has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")

          esac
          echo "has_artifacts=$has_artifacts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent

          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build-artifact:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'

            kind: cli
          - id: macos-x64
            runner: macos-14
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:

      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}

        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"
      - name: Build declared artifact
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Assemble attested product artifacts
    needs: [build-artifact, release-candidate, plan]
    if: always() && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' && needs.build-artifact.result == 'success'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      orchestration_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      # Every matrix target's artifact, so a target added to the matrix cannot be built and then left out of the manifest.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: release-build-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - name: Create exact artifact manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    # !cancelled() not always(): a status function still defeats the skipped-ancestor
    # rule, but cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The release-source checkout alone needs Git credentials because
          # graph-owned tag dispatch pushes from this repository.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Downloaded outside the workspace (under $RUNNER_TEMP, like
      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute
      # re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which requires a
      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      # Needs no secrets: a plain tag push with the checkout's Git credentials, like the release tags. A no-op before 1.0.0.
      - name: Move the floating major tag
        working-directory: release-source
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/move-floating-tag.sh" .callisto/release-decision.json cargo/callisto-cli "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          # Per attempt: keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing the prior one.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

# 2. The committed version decision is the release authority

Status: Accepted (implemented in #54)

## Context

- After the release PR merges, CI must verify the merged release commit before any publish, tag or GitHub release runs (PR #54).
- Before #54 the release roster was derived from the merged commit's raw diff and understood only a direct changeset-to-package match. It rejected any release in which a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling that no changeset named (PR #54; code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`).

## Decision

`callisto version --emit-decision <path>` writes the version decision it computed (package, target version, inclusion reasons) to `<path>`. The managed release-PR action writes it to `.callisto/release-decision.json` by default (`decision_path` input) and commits it in the release PR. After merge, `release plan --from-release-commit --decision <file>` reads that decision and confirms the merged commit's diff matches it exactly, no more and no less. CI never recomputes changeset, group or cascade policy at that boundary. The verified merge is also the authorization: the release workflow has no separate approval gate (no GitHub Environment approval or required reviewers) (incident report §2, requirements 1 and 2; PR #101, "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate").

## Options considered

- **Re-derive cascade and group policy in CI after merge, or keep the raw-diff roster and teach it about groups** — rejected. "Rather than teach the re-derivation about groups -- a second, incomplete reimplementation of changeset/group/cascade resolution -- this trusts the decision `callisto version` already computed and committed … One decision surface instead of two that can drift apart" (PR #54).

## Consequences

- The released roster and versions are exactly those committed in the release PR.
- The decision file is a wire contract. Its schema is versioned: `ReleaseDecisionV1::SCHEMA_VERSION` is 2, and the reader accepts 1 and 2 so an older release PR still plans (commit 7027bbfb0).
- A decision whose entries do not match its own digest fails to decode (E166) before the diff cross-check. The digest is an unkeyed SHA-256, not a signature, so an edit with a recomputed digest that still passes the decoder's roster checks is caught only by the diff cross-check.
- A release commit that does not add or modify the decision file, consumes no changeset, whose manifest versions disagree with the decision, or that leaves a claimed package's changelog untouched is refused (E165). Nothing checks that the decision file was produced by `callisto version --emit-decision`.
- `--emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, then writes its file only after apply succeeds (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs`). A failed apply can leave earlier manifest writes without a decision; interrupted-command recovery is tracked separately.

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `fixed_group_cascade_bump_without_direct_changeset_is_accepted`, `release_plan_rejects_a_commit_whose_manifest_disagrees_with_its_own_decision`, `release_plan_rejects_a_hand_tampered_decision_file`.
- `derive_release_commit_decision` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs` and its unit tests (head mismatch, corrupt decision file, claimed package not observed).

## Revisit when

- Release PRs must be produced by something other than `callisto version` (for example a third-party bot) and cannot carry the decision file.
- A needed check can only be made at merge time from data the decision cannot contain.

## Sources

- PR #54 (7199ad70f), body "Why" section
- Code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs`
- PR #101 (279e32361), squashed commits "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate" and "fix(release): emit the committed release decision"
- Commit 7027bbfb0 (reader accepts schema 1 and 2)
- `crates/callisto-model/src/release/decision.rs` (`decision_digest`, `ReleaseDecisionV1` deserializer)
- Incident report §2 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)
# 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state

Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)

## Context

- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).

## Decision

Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).

## Options considered

- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).

## Consequences

- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
- A registry publish that is complete once its version is visible (npm) is issued and confirmed in two steps within one run: the executor issues every publish it can, lets another npm publish follow an issued one, and confirms the issued publishes together before anything is announced. The issued set lives in memory like the rest of the run; a crash between issue and confirmation leaves the operation unproven, and the rerun observes it first, as for any other effect.
- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index, not when the version is visible (E306, E307).

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.

## Revisit when

- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".

## Sources

- PR #124 (592396564), commit bodies and PR body; closed PR #122
- PR #101 (279e32361): "reject incomplete quiescent execution", "accept an explicit recovery source"
- PR #39 (eeda4a2f5): durable attested execution
- Incident report §2, §6 (F-003), §8 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)
# 4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication

Status: Accepted (implemented in #143)

## Context

- Callisto releases to crates.io, npm, PyPI and GitHub. Each registry has its own auth rules, retries, rate limits and idempotence.
- The original design argued that `cargo` and `npm`/`pnpm` "already do registry auth, retries, rate-limit handling, and idempotence" (docs/00-design.md §9).

## Decision

Callisto decides what to publish and in what order, then runs the ecosystem tool as a subprocess through `CommandRunner`: `cargo`; `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`; `python -m build` then `twine`; `gh`. The tool uses whatever credentials it finds and reports its own auth errors. Before each effect callisto observes provider state itself (`cargo info`, `npm view`, `curl` against the PyPI simple index, `gh api`, `git ls-remote`) and retries only those read-only observations (`retry_observation`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs`). Callisto links no HTTP client crate and runs no credential pre-flight.

## Options considered

- **Native registry clients in callisto** — rejected. The original design argued the tools "already do registry auth, retries, rate-limit handling, and idempotence — reimplementing any of that inside callisto would be redundant and would put callisto in the business of tracking every registry's quirks" (docs/00-design.md §9). §9.5 dropped `octocrab`/`reqwest`/`tokio` from the CLI, which "significantly shrinks the CLI's dependency surface".
- **Credential pre-flight before the first effect** — added in #134, removed in #143: "cargo, npm, twine and gh report their own auth failures, and a rerun adopts every effect that already landed, so a second credential model in Callisto only drifts from the tools'".

## Consequences

- Publishing uses each tool's native authentication. Observation must also reach the same destination: PyPI's curl read is not automatically authenticated by Twine's environment, and private-index route support needs an explicit boundary.
- A missing credential surfaces mid-release as E163 (E164 for `gh`), carrying the tool's redacted stderr. Effects before it have landed; a rerun adopts them (ADR 3).
- Callisto parses tool output to classify results (for example "already published"), so a tool's output change can break classification (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`).
- Every release machine needs the tools on `PATH`.
- Read-only observation retries share a bounded policy, including transient command failures and Retry-After. Private and HTML-only Python index observation is an open decision in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md).

## Enforcement

- None automated. The fixed programs are in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs` (`programs`: git, gh, cargo, npm, curl); the publish programs (pnpm, yarn, bun, `python3` or `python`, twine) are built in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`.
- No HTTP client crate (`reqwest`, `ureq`, `octocrab`, `hyper`) appears in `Cargo.lock`; nothing checks this.

## Revisit when

- A target registry has no CLI that can publish non-interactively.
- A tool's auth failure can leave a registry in a state a rerun cannot adopt.

## Sources

- docs/00-design.md §9, §9.5 (`git show 11038b11b^:docs/00-design.md`)
- PR #134 (3d0e2909d): pre-flight added and widened
- PR #143 (bde7305f9) "refactor!: let tools own auth; one build; lighter release and init", sub-commit "refactor(release)!: drop the local credential pre-flight"
# 8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit

Status: Accepted (implemented in 2c27f8d0b)

## Context

- Callisto rewrites files users own and review: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, changelogs, `pre.json`.
- `--dry-run` is a global flag; `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` and `release execute` reject it (`crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`). "Respect `--dry-run`" was once a convention, and `pre enter`, `pre exit` and `init` forgot it: `pre` wrote `.changeset/pre.json` unconditionally (d15d4c2b0; `crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs`).
- An interrupted run must never leave a partially written file (VER-APPLY-05, `docs/specs/versioning.json`).

## Decision

- TOML edits go through `toml_edit`, changing the existing item in place. `package.json` goes through `serde_json` with `preserve_order`, and indentation, line endings and BOM are detected on read and reproduced on write (`FormatFingerprint`). Callisto-owned JSON such as `pre.json` is regenerated canonically (`crates/callisto-model/src/format/pre.rs`).
- Every file content write goes through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`: temp file in the target's directory, fsync, rename, then fsync the parent and grandparent. Deletions (consumed changesets, `pre.json`) and directory creation use `std::fs` directly.
- Write primitives take `&ApplyPermit`. Its only field is private; outside tests the only constructor is `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)`, which returns `None` on a dry run.

## Options considered

- **Parse into typed structs and serialize back (serde round-trip) for TOML** — reason not recorded. CM.4.1 only says editing the existing item in place, rather than replacing it, "is what makes `toml_edit` preserve comments, blank lines, key order, and inline-table formatting the caller did not touch" (docs/01-spec.md CM.4.1). JSON has no comments, so an order-preserving round trip plus fingerprint is enough (CM.5.1).
- **Regex or line-based edits** — reason not recorded. The rule appears in AGENTS.md invariant 2 without a stated reason.
- **Convention-based dry-run checks** — rejected: "A convention every new write site must remember will eventually be forgotten at one" (`permit.rs`), after `pre` and `init` did (d15d4c2b0). With a permit, a write site has nothing to pass unless its handler minted one (2c27f8d0b).

## Consequences

- TOML manifest diffs in release PRs show only version and dependency-spec changes. `package.json` is re-serialized with serde_json's pretty printer, keeping key order, indentation, line endings, BOM and trailing newline; other layout (for example an inline array) is normalized (`crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs`).
- CRLF manifests and changelogs stay CRLF.
- A failed run can leave earlier files updated; `atomic_write` only prevents a torn single file (VER-APPLY-05).
- Tests need `ApplyPermit::force_for_tests()`, behind `cfg(test)` or the `callisto-model/test-util` feature, enabled only under `[dev-dependencies]`.
- The permit is a type check only. It does not stop code that calls `std::fs` directly, and a handler can still mint one with a literal `false`: `release`, `release artifact-manifest` and `init` do so behind their own dry-run branch (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs`, `init.rs`).

## Enforcement

- Type: `ApplyPermit` (`crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs`), required by `atomic_write` (`crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs`), `Manifest::persist`, changelog writes and the release providers.
- Tests: `crates/callisto-cli/tests/dry_run_invariant_tests.rs` using `assert_no_disk_mutation` (`crates/callisto-fixtures/src/dry_run.rs`); format tests in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` and `npm.rs` (CRLF, BOM, tab indent, comment and decor preservation).

## Revisit when

- A manifest format appears that no format-preserving editor supports.
- Writes must happen outside a command handler that can read the dry-run flag.

## Sources

- Commits 2c27f8d0b and d15d4c2b0 (ApplyPermit introduced; pre and init fixed)
- `crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs` module docs; `crates/callisto-model/Cargo.toml` `test-util` comment
- `docs/specs/versioning.json` VER-APPLY-05
- docs/00-design.md §7.6 step 3; docs/01-spec.md CM.4.1, CM.5.1 (`git show 11038b11b^:docs/<file>`)
- Commit 435c05a17 (shared format fingerprint, CRLF fix)
